title: A Mysterious Figure Appears in Mushoku Tensei Season 3 Episode 11 Preview
content:
Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 revealed the Episode 11 preview images and synopsis ahead of its September 6 premiere. The episode previously revealed its title to be “Turning Point 4,” with fans already ready for it to be another major moment in Rudy’s life. Crunchyroll is streaming the anime as part of its Summer 2026 lineup .

You can see the preview images and synopsis for Episode 11 below.

Having shaken off Atofe’s pursuit, Rudeus and the others manage to obtain Sokas Grass, which is said to be effective against “Dryne Disease.” But will it really cure Nanahoshi’s illness…!? Then, on the night Rudeus finally returns home after a long absence, Man-God (Hitogami) appears and offers him some advice. Just as Rudeus is about to follow it, a mysterious figure suddenly appears…

The main staff for the anime was previously announced and includes:

• Director: Ryosuke Shibuya

• Character Design: Sanae Shimada, Ryota Furukawa

• Music: Yoshiaki Fujisawa

• Studio: Studio Bind

You can also check out the teaser trailer for the ongoing arc below.

Season 3 began with Volume 14, for which Seven Seas describes the story: Nanahoshi, Rudeus, and the rest of their group take a trip to Perugius’s mysterious floating fortress, seeking adventure and a once-in-a-lifetime chance to learn new magic. What they find instead is disaster as one of their number is struck down by a deadly illness. How far will Rudeus go to save a dear friend’s life?

You can also see the key visual for the third season.

The anime is based on a light novel by Rifujin na Magonote with Shirotaka’s illustrations. Seven Seas is publishing the light novel in English. The series is also launching a game titled Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation – Chronicle of Echoes this year. It is a free-to-play game with in-app purchases developed by ASOBIMO.
author: Anime Corner

title: From Far Away TV Anime's New Video Reveals More Cast & Staff, Theme Songs
content:
The official website for the television anime of Kyouko Hikawa 's From Far Away ( Kanata Kara ) shōjo manga presented the anime's main promotional video, key visual, and additional cast and staff members on Wednesday. The video announces and previews the opening theme song "Tōkōkō" by boy group Genin wa Jibun ni Aru. (GNJB), and the ending theme song "Hikari no Gawa de" (At the Side of Light) by four-piece band Nanashi no Tarō .

The newly announced cast members are (Note: Some character names are spelled differently from the manga's English publication by Viz Media ):

• Kimiko Saitō as Gaya

• Tadashi Miyazawa as Gorya

• Taisuke Nakano as Agol

• Miku Itō as Gina Haas

Additional new staff members are:

• Art Director: Masaki Mayuzumi

• Color Key Artist: Imari Katsuragi

• Compositing Director of Photography: Inju Lee

• Editing: Akane Shiraishi

• Sound Director: Satoshi Yano

• Sound Effects: Hidemi Tanaka

• Sound Production: Ai Addiction

Viz Media publishes the manga in English and describes the story:

On her way home from school one day, Noriko is unexpectedly plunged into a strange and extraordinary fantasy world. Her troubles compound exponentially when she is rescued and befriended by a handsome young man by the name of Izark. He may be brave and courageous, but inside Izark lurks the darkest evil imaginable. And according to an ancient prophecy, Noriko possesses the power to unleash that evil. Now, inexorably bound together, these two unlikely allies must navigate a world both wondrous and hostile.

The anime will star (Note: Some character names are spelled differently from the manga's English publication by Viz Media ):

• Tomoyo Kurosawa as Noriko Tachiki

• Kentarō Kumagai as Isaac Kia Taj

• Yūichirō Umehara as Rachev

• Eiji Takeuchi as Kaemos Lee Goda

Noriyuki Abe ( Bleach , Flame of Recca , GTO: Great Teacher Onizuka ) is directing the anime at Studio DEEN . Rika Takasugi ( Ōoku: The Inner Chambers , Yakuza Fiancé: Raise wa Tanin ga Ii ) is in charge of series scripts, Eiji Abiko ( Mr. Osomatsu seasons 3 & 4, Even a Replica Can Fall in Love ) is designing the characters, and Takeshi Hama ( Champignon Witch , Idol Time PriPara ) is composing the music.

The anime will premiere on the Tokyo MX channel on October 4 at 24:00 JST (effectively October 5 at 12 midnight JST), then on October 10 on ABC TV, and on October 13 on WOWOW .

The manga ran in Hakusensha 's LaLa magazine from 1991 to 2002. Hakusensha published the manga's 14th and final compiled book volume in 2003. Hakusensha released the manga's Bunko edition in seven volumes from 2004-2005.

title: Saint Seiya Creator Masami Kurumada Sues Former Manager, Others for 2.8 Billion Yen
content:
Manga creator Masami Kurumada ( Saint Seiya , B'tX , Ring ni Kakero ) announced in a press conference in Tokyo on Wednesday that he has filed a lawsuit against a former board director and others from three of his companies for allegedly misappropriating funds without authorization. He is seeking an estimated 2.8 billion yen (about US$18 million) in damages.

The three companies include Kurumada Productions, which manages the copyrights and merchandising rights of Kurumada's works. According to Kurumada's legal representatives, the former director was also his former manager who was in charge of accounting, and also took part in establishing Kurumada Production. The former manager has known the manga creator for over 15 years.

According to the lawsuit, the defendants at the three companies allegedly misappropriated funds between around 2018 and 2024 by unauthorized transfer of company funds to other accounts, and by having license fee payments transferred to accounts under different company names.

The total misappropriated funds is estimated at 4.6 billion yen (about US$29 million), and Kurumada's legal representatives are seeking 2.8 billion yen in compensation, excluding the 1.8 billion yen (about US$11 million) that has already been repaid.

Kurumada had announced in January 2024 that he would launch the first major exhibition of his manga art in June 2024, but his website announced in March 2024 the cancellation of the exhibition "due to various circumstances."

Kurumada published the original Saint Seiya manga from 1986 to 1990. The manga has inspired a number of television anime, original video anime projects, anime films, and spinoff manga. The original series has 35 million copies in print.

Saint Seiya: Next Dimension - The Myth of Hades (image right) launched in 2006 and ended in July 2024.

Viz Media published the original manga in English under the title Saint Seiya: Knights of the Zodiac . ADV Films released Toei Animation 's anime adaptation with an English dub under the title Knights of the Zodiac , and later released it unedited under the title Saint Seiya . New Video Group later also released the series on DVD.

Knights of the Zodiac: Saint Seiya , the CG anime remake based on the original manga, debuted worldwide in July 2019. Saint Seiya: Knights of the Zodiac - Battle for Sanctuary - , the second season , debuted in July 2021. Saint Seiya: Knights of the Zodiac - Battle for Sanctuary - Part 2 , the next part , premiered in April 2024.

A live-action film of the manga titled Knights of the Zodiac opened in 2023.

Kurumada recently launched the new series Saint Seiya Tenkai-hen ( Saint Seiya : The Heavens Arc) in Akita Shoten 's Weekly Shōnen Champion magazine on May 14.

title: The World's Strongest Rearguard Anime Director Yuji Yanase Dies at 59
content:
Anime director Yuji Yanase, who directed the currently airing The World’s Strongest Rearguard: Labyrinth Country’s Novice Seeker , died on August 22, 2026. He was 59 years old.

The anime’s production committee announced Yanase’s passing on September 2, expressing its condolences and reflecting on his contributions to the series.

“We are deeply saddened by the sudden news of his passing. Director Yanase devoted tremendous effort to the production of The World’s Strongest Rearguard: Labyrinth Country’s Novice Seeker, leading the production team with his passion and warm personality. We would like to express our heartfelt gratitude and offer our deepest condolences.”

MAHO FILM, where Yanase was employed, separately announced that the director died of a myocardial infarction on August 22. According to the studio, his funeral was held privately with close relatives in accordance with his family’s wishes. MAHO FILM also thanked fans and others who supported Yanase during his lifetime.

Yanase had worked as an anime director on numerous productions. His directing credits include By the Grace of the Gods , In the Land of Leadale , If It’s for My Daughter, I’d Even Defeat a Demon Lord , and In Another World with My Smartphone , among other titles.

His latest project, The World’s Strongest Rearguard: Labyrinth Country’s Novice Seeker , is currently ongoing. The fantasy series follows Arihito, who is reincarnated in the Labyrinth Country and takes on the support-focused “Rearguard” class, capable of assisting his party through attack, defense and recovery abilities.

The production committee has not announced any changes to the anime’s broadcast or production schedule in its statement.

title: Main Staff for 'Ikyou no Tsume Nuri Minarai' Announced
content:
Publishing company Shufu to Seikatsusha announced the main staff for the anime adaptation of Murakawa 's Ikyou no Tsume Nuri Minarai ( Apprentice Nail Artist in a Foreign Land ) manga on Wednesday.

Staff Director: Daiji Iwanaga ( Ponkotsu Fuuki Iin to Skirt-take ga Futekisetsu na JK no Hanashi ) Series Composition: Tomoko Konparu ( Kimi ni Todoke ) Script: Tomoko Konparu, Michiko Yokote ( Naruto ) Studio: Zero-G

Marukawa began drawing the isekai fantasy manga in Comic PASH! in March 2022. Shufu to Seikatsusha published the sixth volume in October 2025, with the seventh volume scheduled for a September 4 release.

Tokyopop licensed the manga in English and released the first volume in April 2026. The second volume is scheduled for release on September 8.

title: Director, Animator Yūji Yanase Dies
content:
Director and animator Yūji Yanase died on August 22.

The official website for The Insipid Prince's Furtive Grab for The Throne anime made the announcement on Wednesday. Yanase directed the anime, which premiered on July 6.

Yanase has been working in the anime industry since at least 1988, working as in-between animator for such works as Akira , Kaze o Nuke! , and Doraemon the Movie: Nobita's Dorabian Nights . He was a key animator for such works as Macross 7 , The Legend of Zorro , Tenchi Universe , and Tetsujin 28-go FX . He was animation director on episodes of such works as Saber Marionette J , Fancy Lala , Excel Saga , Hellsing , Chobits , Mezzo , Aria the Animation , and Symphogear , among numerous others.

Yanase made his directorial debut with the 2014 television anime Himegoto , and has since directed such anime as Onsen Yōsei Hakone-chan , In Another World With My Smartphone , If It’s for My Daughter, I’d Even Defeat a Demon Lord , By the Grace of the Gods , In the Land of Leadale , My Unique Skill Makes Me OP even at Level 1 , I’ll Become a Villainess Who Goes Down in History , Apocalypse Bringer Mynoghra , and The World's Strongest Rearguard - Labyrinth Country's Novice Seeker , as well as the aforementioned The Insipid Prince's Furtive Grab for The Throne . He continued working as a key animator, animation director, and episode director in various other productions alongside his directorial duties.

title: Yuuji Yanase, Director of 'Isekai wa Smartphone to Tomo ni.', Dies at 59
content:
Yuuji Yanase , the director behind Isekai wa Smartphone to Tomo ni. ( In Another World With My Smartphone ), died on August 22 due to myocardial infarction. He was 59. A funeral service was held by his close relatives.

Animation studio Maho Film announced the news on Wednesday, where Yanase had been a full-time employee since 2023. The production committee of the ongoing anime series, Saikyou Degarashi Ouji no Anyaku Teii Arasoi ( The Insipid Prince's Furtive Grab for The Throne ), also released a statement regarding his sudden death.

"We are still unable to accept this sudden news and are filled with deep sadness. Director Yanase dedicated tremendous effort to the production of this anime. We offer our most sincere gratitude and heartfelt condolences," the committee shared.

Yanase made his directorial debut in 2017 with Isekai wa Smartphone to Tomo ni. . He was a prominent figure at Maho Film, directing several of the studio's titles, including Uchi no Ko no Tame naraba, Ore wa Moshikashitara Maou mo Taoseru kamo Shirenai. ( If It's for My Daughter, I'd Even Defeat a Demon Lord ), Kami-tachi ni Hirowareta Otoko ( By the Grace of the Gods ), Leadale no Daichi nite ( In the Land of Leadale ), and Level 1 dakedo Unique Skill de Saikyou desu ( My Unique Skill Makes Me OP Even at Level 1 ). He most recently directed Sekai Saikyou no Kouei: Meikyuukoku no Shinjin Tansakusha ( The World's Strongest Rearguard ) in Summer 2026.

title: 3 Drawbacks That Stop Naruto From Becoming The Greatest Anime of All Time
content:
The legacy of the Shonen Big Three remains unmatched even though several years have passed since their debut. As the new era of the anime and manga industry began with shorter and seasonal series, fans appreciate the older generation even more with long-running stories and captivating plots. As one of the biggest Shonen classics, Naruto ‘s influence is unmatched even now. Written and illustrated by Masashi Kishimoto, Naruto became one of the most successful anime and manga franchises of all time. The story of an underdog winning the hearts of those around him and climbing to the top still inspires others.

Naruto raised an entire generation of anime fans who followed the protagonist’s journey from the beginning to the end. However, as a long-running show, it’s impossible for Naruto to be flawless. Due to years of broadcast, the anime suffered from pacing issues and inconsistent animation. Not only that, but since the manga was also serialized weekly, the anime had to release several filler episodes in between. However, apart from this, there are other drawbacks that stop Naruto from becoming the greatest anime despite having such an exceptional story.

3. Naruto ‘s Underwhelming Female Cast Is One of The Worst in Shonen

Action Shonen has never been famous for having a great female cast, with the few exceptions of One Piece and Bleach. Since the demographic primarily focuses on a young male audience, most creators are infamous for an underwhelming female cast. However, even among those series, Naruto stands out as one of the worst. While there are exceptions with powerful female characters such as Sakura and Tsunade, it takes a lot more than physical strength for character writing to be good. Most of the female characters other than them are often sidelined with little to no plot relevance.

Naruto’s side characters and villains are often considered exceptional, including Itachi, Madara, Nagato, and more. However, with most of the well-written characters being male, the female characters are often sidelined. Even the final villain, Kaguya Otsutsuki , is so controversial that she rarely has any fans. For a series as big as Naruto, having an unpopular final villain is a major flaw in terms of writing and delivery of the plotline.

2. The Unresolved Storylines Are Still Disappointing

Naruto still causes confusion with many unresolved storylines and unanswered questions. Hashirama’s fate is so famously overlooked in the story that many fans just convinced themselves that the character was so powerful, it was impossible to write how he died. Regardless, a legendary character like him deserved a better ending than fans having to guess what really happened to him.

However, that’s just one example, but there are several instances where the story failed to answer major questions, including the power systems and many other plot points. Whether it was Itachi’s illness or Orochimaru’s sudden change of heart, a lot of the things could be explored better. The final stretch of the story in particular felt rushed with so many things happening all at once.

1. The Plot Twist With The Final Villain Will Forever Keep Fans Divided

There’s really no way to sugarcoat that the finale is still one of the most divisive moments in anime history. After hyping Madara Uchiha as the finale villain of the story, he turned out to be nothing more than a puppet of Black Zetsu. Madara’s actions were guided by Zetsu in order to free Kaguya Otsutsuki from the eternal prison her sons put her into centuries ago. Even now, the ending often receives mixed reactions, especially in the manga that doesn’t feature an epilogue after the final war.

Kaguya’s last-minute appearance shifted the flow of the story when it was just reaching its finale. With Obito joining Naruto’s side and Madara regretting his decisions, they became victims of Zetsu despite the war they started and the countless lives they took. Not to mention that Kaguya’s appearance happened with zero narrative buildup, and it seemed more like a quick way to set up the story of a sequel rather than ending the main story when it should have.

Most of the female characters other than them are often sidelined with little to no plot relevance.

Naruto’s side characters and villains are often considered exceptional, including Itachi, Madara, Nagato, and more. However, with most of the well-written characters being male, the female characters are often sidelined. Even the final villain, Kaguya Otsutsuki , is so controversial that she rarely has any fans. For a series as big as Naruto, having an unpopular final villain is a major flaw in terms of writing and delivery of the plotline.
2. The Unresolved Storylines Are Still Disappointing

Naruto still causes confusion with many unresolved storylines and unanswered questions. Hashirama’s fate is so famously overlooked in the story that many fans just convinced themselves that the character was so powerful, it was impossible to write how he died. Regardless, a legendary character like him deserved a better ending than fans having to guess what really happened to him.

However, that’s just one example, but there are several instances where the story failed to answer major questions, including the power systems and many other plot points. Whether it was Itachi’s illness or Orochimaru’s sudden change of heart, a lot of the things could be explored better. The final stretch of the story in particular felt rushed with so many things happening all at once.
1. The Plot Twist With The Final Villain Will Forever Keep Fans Divided

There’s really no way to sugarcoat that the finale is still one of the most divisive moments in anime history. After hyping Madara Uchiha as the finale villain of the story, he turned out to be nothing more than a puppet of Black Zetsu. Madara’s actions were guided by Zetsu in order to free Kaguya Otsutsuki from the eternal prison her sons put her into centuries ago. Even now, the ending often receives mixed reactions, especially in the manga that doesn’t feature an epilogue after the final war.

Kaguya’s last-minute appearance shifted the flow of the story when it was just reaching its finale. With Obito joining Naruto’s side and Madara regretting his decisions, they became victims of Zetsu despite the war they started and the countless lives they took. Not to mention that Kaguya’s appearance happened with zero narrative buildup, and it seemed more like a quick way to set up the story of a sequel rather than ending the main story when it should have.

title: Building the Dark Fantasy "Sentenced to Be a Hero" with Studio KAI
content:
Studio KAI was founded in 2019, and their name "KAI" means "oar" in Japanese. Since an oar is a tool used when rowing a boat, Studio KAI's mission is to row boldly into the endless ocean of animation with passion and determination. The result of this is the breathtaking character acting and jaw-dropping action that we saw in Sentenced to Be a Hero .

On Day 2 of Anime Expo, the creative minds behind Sentenced to Be a Hero discussed the adaptation which captivated fans from all over the world with its rich and dark fantasy world where the scent of death lingers.

Guests: Yoshiki Nakakouji (Assistant Director and Creature Designer) Yasutaka Kimura (Chief Animation Direction) Takeru Noda (Character Designer) Masashi Masuo (Animation Producer)

Note: MyAnimeList also had the opportunity to send a few follow up questions after the panel!

Kinetic Action

──Nakakouji-san, as Sentenced to Be a Hero 's assistant director, what was your approach to making the action scenes have such immersion and impact?

Yoshiki Nakakouji: First of all, thank you to everyone who watched the first season.

Although he's not here at the panel today, I often talked with the director, Hiroyuki Takashima, about how we don't want to create action just for the sake of action. The idea is that as the story progresses, the character's emotions change before and after certain events, and the action animation serves as a technique to effectively depict those changes.

Throughout the entire series, our goal was to convey situations through visuals rather than relying on the dialogue or monologues. This is why during the action scenes, we paid close attention to the characters' expressions, reactions, sense of weight, and overall visual clarity of each shot.

We were also highly particular about the first-person perspective action scenes that appear frequently throughout the series. For example, in episode 1, we incorporated POV shots using various techniques such as 3D mapping and hand-drawn background animation.

Through these methods, I think we were able to bring the realism and intensity of this dark, fictional world right to the viewer.

Vividly Alive Characters

──Noda-san, could you tell us about your core philosophy when animating characters?

Takeru Noda: The thing I was most conscious of when designing the characters for the Sentenced to Be a Hero anime was the facial expressions and nuanced gestures of each character. As human beings, we don't have a one-dimensional set of expressions or gestures. Rather, our complex inner emotions inevitably pile up and manifest themselves on the surface.

To transform a verbal story filled with fantastical elements into a convincing drama, it was important to treat these characters like real people with human-like expressions and gestures. While I correct as many cuts as possible as an animation director, I can't fix every cut. So when creating the character design reference sheets, I made sure to emphasize their standing postures and various expressions so that our entire animation staff could instantly grasp the characters' personalities.

──Kimura-san, as a chief animation director, what specific details did you focus on?

Yasutaka Kimura: Given the creative direction, just as Noda-san mentioned, I focused on creating silhouettes and character acting that were instantly recognizable. To achieve that, I needed to deeply understand their personalities, what kind of past they have, their hobbies and preferences, as well as their regrets. I also needed to know what kind of future awaits them. To firmly lay that foundation, I constantly reread the original light novels to deepen my understanding of the characters.

Rather than relying on standard textbook anime acting, I think we were able to incorporate nuanced movements that make the audience think, "Yeah, this character would definitely do that." Of course, this applied not just to the main cast, but to the faeries, the demon blights, the colorful background characters—even down to the smoke, explosions, and the gory, brutal scenes. We aimed to connect the characters' emotions with their environment to create cohesive, convincing visuals.

Building an Unforgiving World

──Nakakouji-san, what did you focus on when animating the ruined cities, harsh battlefields, and overall atmosphere of this particular world?

Yoshiki Nakakouji: For this series, there were two things the creative team aimed for alongside the background art team. First, it was to depict a true dark fantasy world and second, to utilize the play of light and shadow for storytelling.

To depict a dark fantasy world, we used Northern Europe as a real-world reference to express a cold, stark atmosphere. After finishing the setting, thanks to the ideas from our world-building designer Nobutaka Ike, we paid special attention to how the sky was depicted. I think figuring out how to express the darkness and coldness while portraying a gruesome and cruel world was truly the central theme of this production.

Regarding the latter, when utilizing light and shadow for storytelling, we worked closely with our art director Yuusuke Watanabe and color designer Hiroko Umezaki to carefully craft the lighting, shadow, and color palette of the town. I think the striking colors and background art in the final episode represents what the director and our team set out to achieve.

Grotesque, Colossal Creatures

──Nakakouji-san, how did you bring these terrifying monsters with such overwhelming presence to life as tangible horrors rather than generic enemies?

Yoshiki Nakakouji: When director Takashima and I were brainstorming the creature designs, we decided to build everything around the word "nightmare," which is a huge keyword in the original novels. Rather than going for something simply powerful or cool, we wanted them to appear truly alien and deeply unsettling within the world.

So we started with the keyword "nightmare," and we used eyes as a shared motif. Specifically, every demon blight shares the same eye motif as its defining feature, while the faeries are designed with their eyes completely covered by slime mold. Also, to keep the fantasy world grounded, we used real-world organisms as our design inspiration instead of just making up completely imaginary monsters.

MyAnimeList's Questions

──Looking back on the first season, is there a scene that best represents the kind of series you wanted Sentenced to Be a Hero to be, and what makes that moment stand out to you?

Nakakouji: I would actually choose two scenes.

The first is the opening sequence of episode 1, from Dotta's escape through Couveunge Forest to the moment Xylo comes to his rescue. The second is the scene in the final episode where Patausche kills Marlen in his room.

The episode 1 sequence remains especially memorable because it represented our first fully realized vision of what Sentenced to Be a Hero should look and feel like. We spent a great deal of time experimenting and feeling our way through the process, so seeing that vision come together left a lasting impression on me.

As for the final episode, it showcased the artistic "scheme" developed through the director's vision and realized through the combined efforts of the art, color design, and animation teams. It was a particularly distinctive style of direction, and the fact that we were able to achieve it during the final episode, despite having extremely limited resources at that stage, left me with a genuine sense of relief and satisfaction. I remember thinking, "Thank goodness we pulled it off" (laughs) .

Kimura: The scene that stands out most to me is the ending of episode 12, where Patausche is sentenced to be a hero.

One of the central themes of Sentenced to Be a Hero is Xylo's struggle to overcome his trauma, inner conflicts, and anger, ultimately surpassing himself. In contrast, Patausche is gradually consumed by her doubts, pride, and sense of identity, and is pushed into a situation where she too must transcend herself. While the two characters are opposites in many ways, they each embody a different color of despair, and I find that contrast particularly compelling.

In a world defined almost entirely by despair, when Patausche finally drives a sword into her own neck, I felt what I can only describe as a "nightmarish hope." To me, that "nightmarish hope" captures the essence of the world of Sentenced to Be a Hero more vividly than anything else.

──Masuo-san, from your perspective as the animation producer, what made Sentenced to Be a Hero a particularly unique project to work on?

Masuo: One of the defining characteristics of this series is its extremely dark world, where humanity's habitable territory has been reduced to only a very limited area. We worked hard to ensure that viewers could immediately sense this atmosphere simply by looking at the backgrounds and overall visual presentation.

Director Takahashi and Ike, who was responsible for the world-building, carefully developed every aspect of the setting in great detail. As a result, every frame came to embody what people would instantly recognize as the world of Sentenced to Be a Hero . Maintaining that level of quality and preserving the show's distinctive atmosphere was incredibly challenging, but I believe the effort resulted in something truly unlike any other anime.

Another unique aspect was the creatures featured throughout the series. Their designs were unlike anything we had seen before, and their presence helped deepen and enrich the world-building even further.

──Was there a character or moment that you unexpectedly grew attached to while working on the series?

Masuo: The most memorable part of the production for me was episode 12. At the time, the schedule was under tremendous pressure, and one of our greatest concerns was figuring out how we could possibly bring the episode together under those circumstances. However, the director took the lead by presenting clear and concrete creative solutions, guiding the entire team through the process. The finished result ultimately became something genuinely moving.

What impressed me most was that the final version far exceeded what I had originally envisioned during the scenario development stage. The director consistently communicated his vision to the staff, from environmental design and character shading to the subtle nuances of the performances. I believe that unwavering commitment to a clear creative direction is what enabled episode 12 to achieve such a remarkable level of quality.

Nakakouji: It's not exactly that I was surprised by it, but as the production process became increasingly intense, there were many moments when both the staff and I personally felt pushed to our limits. I imagine that's true of almost any production environment (laughs) .

Whenever that happened, however, I found myself gaining a deeper understanding of the heroes sentenced to punishment, especially their unique, almost unhinged sense of heroism and their deeply personal motivations. The more I understood them, the more I empathized with them, and the more attached I became to each character.

That experience was something refreshingly new in my career, and it remains one of the most memorable aspects of working on this project.

Kimura: In terms of personality and humanity, Xylo is definitely my favorite character. I was particularly moved by his line in the second half of episode 6: "I want to believe I'm not done for yet." The fact that he still refuses to give up on himself in such a harsh world is something I deeply respect as a fellow man.

Of course, I like Xylo, but surprisingly, I also grew very fond of Venetim. It was a lot of fun making such a handsome, composed-looking character perform embarrassing and pathetic moments (laughs) .

• Looking to Season 2

──Masuo-san, could you share Studio KAI's vision for the future, along with a final message for all the amazing fans who gathered here at AX?

Masashi Masuo: We give all our thanks to our incredible fans around the world who supported season one. Because of you all, we are able to bring you season two. We’re truly grateful.

In season two, we're diving way deeper into the dynamic between Xylo and Teoritta with fiercer battles for the penal hero unit, and with even more terrifying new creatures and battlefields on a massive scale. The entire team at Studio KAI is pushing their limits to deliver a season that exceeds your expectations. We will continue to give our all to bring you even more excitement and unforgettable stories.

Beyond Sentenced to Be a Hero , we're actively tackling major new titles and original projects and hope that you'll enjoy them. Please keep rooting for Xylo and the Studio KAI team, and keep supporting us on our journey!

This panel was conducted through an interpreter and has been edited for clarity.

Watch Yuusha-kei ni Shosu (Sentenced to Be a Hero) on: https://www.crunchyroll.com/series/GT00356809/

title: Crunchyroll’s Biggest Isekai Unveils New Look At Beloved Characters For a Major Project
content:
Isekai series have been gaining more popularity in recent years, and among them, Re:Zero − Starting Life in Another World stands out as one of the best in the industry. The series often stands out for its dark themes and unique plot, especially among Crunchyroll anime. The anime is based on an acclaimed light novel written by Tappei Nagatsuki and illustrated by Shinichiro Ootsuka, which has been ongoing since 2014 and is nowhere near its ending. 2026 is a crucial year for fans with the premiere of Season 4, where the story takes another dark turn. The anime went on a brief hiatus in June this year after releasing Episode 11 of the fourth season. Just like every other season of Re:Zero , Season 4 is also streaming on Crunchyroll, the largest platform for anime fans across the globe.

However, while Season 4 prepares for its ending with the Recapture Arc, the official X handle of the series just confirmed a pop-up shop event that coincides with Emilia’s birthday. The pop-up shop also shares a new visual featuring Subaru, Emilia, and Beatrice. The visual features them in different attire than what anime fans are used to seeing. It will be held on September 23rd, 2026, in Japan. The official X handle also shares a link to reveal all the updates fans need for this upcoming event.

Re:Zero − Starting Life in Another World Season 4 Will Conclude in September 2026

The fourth season premiered in April this year as part of the Spring 2026 lineup. Following the broadcast of Episode 11, the anime went on a hiatus for a few weeks and returned with new episodes in August. The new episodes feature the Recapture Arc from the light novel, one of the best parts of the story.

The anime returned to Crunchyroll on a weekly schedule. Additionally, while the first cour of the fourth season released subbed and dubbed episodes simultaneously, the second cour faced a two-week delay in the English dub . The anime is set to conclude its latest season on September 30th, 2026, with Episode 19. Fans will also get an update on the upcoming season once Season 4 reaches its conclusion.

What’s Happening in Re:Zero − Starting Life in Another World Season 4?

The first cour of the ongoing season adapted the Loss Arc, where Subaru lost his memories and dealt with intense paranoia and isolation. After going through such a difficult ordeal, he is more than ready to fight again in the Recapture Arc . There’s no doubt that Season 4 is by far the most intense the story has ever been.

The anime has never shied away from high stakes, tragedy, and overwhelmingly dangerous incidents, but the situation is far graver this time around. Subaru was forced to witness his friends die in gruesome ways, forcing him to realize his own weakness and inability to stop those tragedies from happening. The Recapture Arc focuses on the aftermath of the Loss Arc, where Subaru and the others are in a major battle against the Sin Archbishop of Gluttony.
